metric.name: clamp bridge support proxy per volume

instruction: FreeCAD quantified CAD optimization task. Before starting the work, launch FreeCAD from `/usr/bin/freecad` and open `baseline.stl` there. Open /home/user/Desktop/baseline.stl and /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf in FreeCAD, use them as the starting geometry and footprint guide, and redesign the part as a lightweight load-bearing fixture. This is a continuous-score optimization task, not a request to match one hidden answer. Case: cable clamp saddle bridge. Objective: Maximize clamp bridge support per volume while preserving two saddle supports and a center cable load zone. Required output: /home/user/Desktop/optimized.stl. Hard constraints: keep the STL within envelope [92.0, 58.0, 34.0] mm, keep bounding-box spans at least [86.0, 52.0, 18.0] mm, keep volume between 12500.0 and 66000.0 mm^3, and preserve at least 95% sampled material coverage in every support/load prism marked in /home/user/Desktop/profile.dxf and fully specified in /home/user/Desktop/constraints.json (support prisms extend from z=0 to 13.0 mm; load prisms extend from z=0 to 18.0 mm). The optimized STL must be one connected, watertight, consistently oriented solid. The evaluator parses only the real optimized.stl geometry, computes three-dimensional required-zone coverage and this continuous metric: clamp bridge support proxy / volume; transverse saddle span and cable load-zone coverage drive the score. It writes score.json and quant_metrics.json, and ignores any self-reported score. Do not read or copy ground_truth and do not edit eval.py.
